lessons.title: Close-up: hand, hair, face and skirt

zoom.label: Her bent right forearm and hand in front of her chest, above the belt

c1.text: Level one: she stands still, feet together. Now zoom to the one diagonal in her body: her right arm.

zoom.label: Her bent right forearm and hand in front of her chest, above the belt

c1q.text: What is her right hand doing?

sources.title: Étienne Michon, 'Musée du Louvre', Journal des Savants 7 (September 1909), p. 422 (our translation)

correction.truth: The hand is open and lies flat on her chest.
correction.evidence: The crop; the Louvre's 1909 report: the right hand brought to the chest.

c1b.text: Yes. Her open hand lies flat across her chest, fingers together. It is the only gesture she makes.

c1c.text: Her arm is folded, not raised.

correction.tempting: Her hand is up near her shoulder.
correction.truth: The forearm crosses her body and the hand rests on her chest.
correction.evidence: The crop; the Louvre's 1909 report: the right hand brought to the chest.

c1m.text: One hand on the chest: her only gesture.

zoom.label: The lower ends of her long layered locks, on each side of her neck

c2.text: Level one: her hair is cut into layers like steps. Now zoom to where the locks stop, over her chest.

zoom.label: The lower ends of her long layered locks, on each side of her neck

c2q.text: How do her long locks end?

sources.title: Musée du Louvre, collection record Ma 3098 (MND 847), 'Dame d'Auxerre' (our translations)
Mark D. Fullerton, Greek Sculpture (Chichester: Wiley-Blackwell, 2016), chapter 1, publisher's excerpt

correction.tempting: They hang at her neck like beads.
correction.truth: They are the ends of her locks, tied off.

c2b.text: Nothing is loose: every lock is tied.

correction.truth: Each lock ends in a small tied tip.

c2c.text: Yes. Each layered lock tapers to a tied tip over her chest.

c2m.text: Layered locks, tied at the tips.

zoom.label: Her face, framed by the layered hair

c3.text: Level one: nobody knows whom she shows. Now zoom to her face.

zoom.label: Her face, framed by the layered hair

c3q.text: What has happened to her face?

sources.title: Musée du Louvre, collection record Ma 3098 (MND 847), 'Dame d'Auxerre' (our translations)

c3a.text: Yes. One side keeps its eye and nose; the other has broken off, leaving rough stone.

correction.truth: That side of the face is missing; the stone has broken away.

correction.tempting: The two halves differ in tone.
correction.truth: The left part of her face is missing.

c3m.text: A face half lost, and a name never known.

zoom.label: The front of her long skirt, below the knees

c4.text: Level one: traces of red paint survive on her bust. Now zoom to the front of her long skirt.

zoom.label: The front of her long skirt, below the knees

c4q.text: What is cut into the front of her skirt?

sources.title: Musée du Louvre, collection record Ma 3098 (MND 847), 'Dame d'Auxerre' (our translations)
Mark D. Fullerton, Greek Sculpture (Chichester: Wiley-Blackwell, 2016), chapter 1, publisher's excerpt

correction.truth: They are patterns on her dress; the Louvre lists no inscription.

c4b.text: Yes. Fine incised lines make squares inside squares down the skirt, part of the dress pattern. They were once coloured.

correction.truth: The lines were incised on purpose to decorate the dress.

c4m.text: Squares cut into stone, once filled with colour.

c1q.what_you_learn: Her right hand lies open and flat across her chest, her only gesture.
